frames.frame: Contrary to [what S might think / the perception that [S V]], [主句]
frames.gloss: 与（人们可能以为的/某种普遍看法）相反，……

examples.text: Contrary to what some people might think, I don't get paid to travel—I simply choose the lifestyle.

Contrary to the perception that he works under a mango tree in a tropical haven, Adams says the reality of this life means that he often ends up staying in more western style places in globalised cities—ones that are sure to have air conditioning and a decent connection—rather than exotic beachfront cafés.
As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster.
As much as that sounds like a politically correct TV advertisement, it's great that that's the time we're in now.
Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced.
In other words, no one speaks “standard English”; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.

frames.gloss: 以一种……的方式（that从句修饰way）
frames.notes: that为定语从句引导词，非其他功能

examples.text: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual’s underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
They are borderless, mostly self-employed remote workers who interact with cities in a way that's entirely different from a tourist, but still doesn't quite reach the status of resident.

frames.gloss: 「……这一发现/事实」+谓语：该发现表明/令人担忧
frames.notes: 同位语从句作长主语，主谓分离易误读
frames.related: the [抽象名词] that [S V]（同位语 that 从句）

examples.text: The finding that the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media is extremely concerning.
Although the research does not prove that social media causes depression, the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated.

frames.gloss: 急于/热衷做某事的（人或机构），后置修饰

examples.text: Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too- easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services.
You can take note of how much carbon dioxide your forest is capturing and sell carbon credits to companies keen to offset their emissions.

frames.notes: 括号对内嵌定义，跳读易丢信息
frames.related: what we call / what are known as [X]

examples.text: These targets include both the rehabilitation of forested areas that have lost density or look a bit weak (a process known as 'restoration' in forestry jargon) and the recovery of forest cover in areas where it was completely cleared (what's known as 'reforestation').

Although not technically reforestation, agroforestry (a system of land use in which harvestable trees or shrubs are grown among or around crops or on pasture land, as a means of preserving or enhancing the productivity of the land) provides an opportunity for small-holder farmers to sustain their livelihoods while adding some forest cover to their farms.

candidates.gloss: 一项接一项（研究）反复表明……

examples.text: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences.

candidates.frame: It's been [时间] since [S did], but [主句]

examples.text: It’s been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn’t gone away.
It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.

candidates.frame: could not be/have a more [Adj] [N] than [B]
candidates.gloss: 再没有比……更……的了（逆说最高级）

examples.text: The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City.
The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.

However inconvenient, a trip to a local doctor, immigration office or laundry—or a conflict with a local Airbnb host (the accommodation style of choice for most nomads)—can be far more culturally instructive than a trip to the national museum.

candidates.frame: A is not necessarily [X], but neither is B

examples.text: Travel isn't necessarily required for them to do their jobs, but neither is staying in one place.

candidates.gloss: ……，而……只有其一半（对照数据回声）

examples.text: Research found that two in five girls are on social media for at least three hours a day—with half as many boys engaged to the same extent.
About half of affected girls suffered disrupted sleep, compared with 20% of depressed boys.

candidates.gloss: 同样将于今年出台的是……（表语前置倒装）

examples.text: Also due this year is information commissioner Elizabeth Denham's Age Appropriate Design Code, covering the use of children's personal data.

candidates.gloss: 比（某国/某地）还要多出……（规模锚定）
candidates.notes: 以地名为规模参照，2961同族“the size of+地名”

examples.text: By 2030, the goal is to reach 350 million hectares—20% more land than India.
Is it something that runs on internal energy that is spent with use?
Or is it something that is bolstered as you apply it and persist?

candidates.gloss: 有时是……，有时则是……（因时而异）

examples.text: Sometimes, it's the ability to resist temptation, such as distractions to avoid a particular task.
Other times it's the ability to persist with a task when your energy and motivation seem low.
